description: A dazzling megacity where ancient temples sit beside neon-lit skyscrapers. Tokyo offers unmatched food culture, from Michelin-starred sushi to ¥500 ramen. Cherry blossom season and autumn foliage make it magical year-round.

attractions.name: Senso-ji Temple
attractions.description: Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple in the heart of Asakusa.

attractions.name: Shibuya Crossing
attractions.description: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing — iconic Tokyo energy.

attractions.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
attractions.description: Fresh sushi, street food, and Japanese kitchen knives.

attractions.name: Meiji Shrine
attractions.description: Peaceful Shinto shrine surrounded by forest in central Tokyo.

attractions.name: TeamLab Borderless
attractions.description: Immersive digital art museum — stunning interactive exhibits.

attractions.name: Golden Gai
attractions.description: Narrow alleyways packed with tiny themed bars in Shinjuku.

restaurants.name: Ichiran Ramen
restaurants.description: Famous solo-dining ramen chain with customizable noodles.

restaurants.name: Sushi Dai
restaurants.description: Legendary sushi counter near Tsukiji — worth the queue.

restaurants.name: Gonpachi Nishi-Azabu
restaurants.description: The restaurant that inspired Kill Bill's fight scene.

restaurants.name: Afuri
restaurants.description: Light, citrusy yuzu shio ramen — a modern classic.

hotels.name: Park Hyatt Tokyo
hotels.description: Iconic luxury hotel featured in Lost in Translation.

hotels.name: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku
hotels.description: Great location with a Godzilla head on the roof.

hotels.name: Khaosan Tokyo Kabuki
hotels.description: Fun, social hostel in Asakusa — great for solo travellers.

travel_tips: Get a Suica card for seamless train travel.
Carry cash — many small restaurants are cash only.
Bow slightly when greeting people.
Convenience stores (konbini) have excellent cheap meals.
safety_notes: Extremely safe. Japan has one of the lowest crime rates in the world.

description: The City of Light captivates with world-class art, romantic boulevards, and pastries that defy description. Every arrondissement tells a different story, from the bohemian Marais to the elegant Champs-Élysées.

attractions.name: Eiffel Tower
attractions.description: The icon of Paris — sunset views from the second floor are unforgettable.

attractions.name: Louvre Museum
attractions.description: Home to the Mona Lisa and 35,000 other works of art.

attractions.name: Montmartre & Sacré-Cœur
attractions.description: Hilltop artists' quarter with panoramic city views.

attractions.name: Seine River Cruise
attractions.description: See Paris from the water at golden hour.

attractions.name: Le Marais
attractions.description: Historic district with boutiques, falafel, and vibrant nightlife.

restaurants.name: Le Bouillon Chartier
restaurants.description: Stunning belle-époque dining hall serving affordable French classics since 1896.

restaurants.name: Breizh Café
restaurants.description: The best crêpes and galettes in Paris — Cancale butter is the secret.

restaurants.name: L'As du Fallafel
restaurants.description: Legendary falafel in the Marais — huge portions, always a queue.

restaurants.name: Le Comptoir du Panthéon
restaurants.description: Classic brasserie overlooking the Panthéon.

hotels.name: Hôtel Plaza Athénée
hotels.description: Legendary palace hotel on Avenue Montaigne.

hotels.name: Hôtel Jeanne d'Arc Le Marais
hotels.description: Charming hotel in the heart of the Marais.

hotels.name: Generator Paris
hotels.description: Stylish hostel near Canal Saint-Martin.

travel_tips: Buy a carnet of 10 metro tickets to save money.
Museums are free on the first Sunday of each month.
Tipping is included in the bill but rounding up is appreciated.
Learn basic French phrases — locals appreciate the effort.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Watch for pickpockets at tourist hotspots and on the metro.

description: A sensory overload in the best way — ornate temples, chaotic markets, rooftop bars, and street food that costs almost nothing. Bangkok is where backpackers and luxury travellers intersect.

attractions.name: Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew
attractions.description: Dazzling royal palace and Thailand's most sacred temple.

attractions.name: Chatuchak Weekend Market
attractions.description: 15,000 stalls — the world's largest outdoor market.

attractions.name: Wat Arun
attractions.description: Temple of Dawn — stunning at sunset from across the river.

attractions.name: Chinatown (Yaowarat)
attractions.description: Neon-lit street food paradise — best after dark.

attractions.name: Sky Bar at Lebua
attractions.description: Rooftop bar from The Hangover II — spectacular city views.

restaurants.name: Jay Fai
restaurants.description: Street food legend with a Michelin star — try the crab omelette.

restaurants.name: Pad Thai Thip Samai
restaurants.description: Bangkok's most famous pad Thai — wrapped in a crispy egg.

restaurants.name: Som Tam Nua
restaurants.description: Incredible papaya salad and fried chicken in Siam Square.

hotels.name: Mandarin Oriental Bangkok
hotels.description: Historic riverside luxury — hosted writers and royalty since 1876.

hotels.name: Ibis Styles Bangkok Sukhumvit 4
hotels.description: Modern hotel near Nana BTS — great value.

hotels.name: NapPark Hostel
hotels.description: Stylish capsule hostel near Khao San Road.

travel_tips: Use the BTS Skytrain to avoid traffic jams.
Negotiate tuk-tuk prices before getting in.
Dress modestly when visiting temples (cover knees and shoulders).
Street food is safe — look for busy stalls with high turnover.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Beware of common tourist scams (gem shops, closed temple trick).

description: The Eternal City layers 2,800 years of history with la dolce vita. Every cobblestone street leads to a piazza, a ruin, or a gelato shop. The food alone is worth the flight.

attractions.name: Colosseum
attractions.description: Ancient amphitheatre where gladiators fought — book skip-the-line tickets.

attractions.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
attractions.description: Michelangelo's ceiling and one of the world's greatest art collections.

attractions.name: Trastevere
attractions.description: Charming medieval neighbourhood — the best area for evening dining.

attractions.name: Trevi Fountain
attractions.description: Baroque masterpiece — toss a coin and you'll return to Rome.

attractions.name: Pantheon
attractions.description: 2,000-year-old temple with a perfect concrete dome — free entry.

restaurants.name: Da Enzo al 29
restaurants.description: Tiny Trastevere trattoria — best cacio e pepe in Rome.

restaurants.name: Pizzarium
restaurants.description: Gabriele Bonci's legendary pizza al taglio — crispy, creative toppings.

restaurants.name: Roscioli
restaurants.description: Deli-restaurant hybrid with incredible pasta and wine selection.

hotels.name: Hotel de Russie
hotels.description: Rocco Forte luxury between the Spanish Steps and Piazza del Popolo.

hotels.name: Hotel Santa Maria
hotels.description: Peaceful courtyard hotel in Trastevere — orange trees included.

hotels.name: The Yellow Hostel
hotels.description: Lively hostel near Termini with a rooftop bar.

travel_tips: Book Colosseum and Vatican tickets online in advance.
Avoid restaurants right on major piazzas — tourist prices.
Carry a water bottle — Rome has free drinking fountains (nasoni) everywhere.
Rome is very walkable — don't bother with taxis for central sights.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Watch for pickpockets on buses and at tourist sites.

description: The city that never sleeps delivers on every cliché. World-class museums, Broadway shows, food from every culture on earth, and an energy that's impossible to replicate anywhere else.

attractions.name: Central Park
attractions.description: 843 acres of green in the middle of Manhattan — walk, bike, or boat.

attractions.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
attractions.description: One of the world's largest art museums — pay what you wish for NY residents.

attractions.name: Brooklyn Bridge Walk
attractions.description: Iconic walk across the East River with skyline views.

attractions.name: Broadway Show
attractions.description: See a world-class musical or play in the Theatre District.

attractions.name: High Line
attractions.description: Elevated park on a former railway — great for a sunset stroll.

restaurants.name: Joe's Pizza
restaurants.description: Classic New York slice in Greenwich Village since 1975.

restaurants.name: Xi'an Famous Foods
restaurants.description: Hand-pulled noodles with spicy cumin lamb — addictive.

restaurants.name: Peter Luger Steak House
restaurants.description: Brooklyn's legendary steakhouse since 1887 — cash only.

restaurants.name: Los Tacos No. 1
restaurants.description: Authentic Mexican tacos in Chelsea Market.

hotels.name: The Plaza
hotels.description: Legendary luxury on the corner of Central Park.

hotels.name: Pod 51
hotels.description: Micro-rooms, great location in Midtown — smart budget choice.

hotels.name: HI New York City Hostel
hotels.description: Huge hostel on the Upper West Side near Central Park.

travel_tips: Get a 7-day unlimited MetroCard if staying more than 3 days.
Broadway TKTS booth sells same-day discount tickets.
Walk everywhere in Manhattan — it's faster than you think.
Tip 18-20% at restaurants — it's expected, not optional.
safety_notes: Generally safe in tourist areas. Stay aware late at night in less-busy neighborhoods.

description: Gaudí's surreal architecture, golden beaches, and tapas bars that stay open until 3am. Barcelona blends Catalan culture, Mediterranean lifestyle, and avant-garde art into something completely unique.

attractions.name: Sagrada Família
attractions.description: Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece — book tickets for the towers.

attractions.name: Park Güell
attractions.description: Colourful mosaic park with panoramic city views.

attractions.name: La Boqueria Market
attractions.description: Famous food market on Las Ramblas — incredible fresh produce and juices.

attractions.name: Barceloneta Beach
attractions.description: City beach with chiringuitos (beach bars) and seafood.

attractions.name: Gothic Quarter
attractions.description: Medieval streets full of hidden squares, bars, and street art.

restaurants.name: Cal Pep
restaurants.description: Legendary tapas bar — sit at the counter for the full experience.

restaurants.name: La Boqueria Pinotxo Bar
restaurants.description: Tiny counter bar inside the market — chickpeas, fried egg, perfection.

restaurants.name: Can Culleretes
restaurants.description: Barcelona's oldest restaurant (1786) — classic Catalan dishes.

hotels.name: Hotel Arts Barcelona
hotels.description: Beachfront luxury with Frank Gehry's golden fish sculpture.

hotels.name: Hotel Brummell
hotels.description: Hip boutique hotel in Poble-sec with a rooftop pool.

hotels.name: Sant Jordi Hostels Sagrada Família
hotels.description: Social hostel with a pool — right near the Sagrada Família.

travel_tips: Book Sagrada Família tickets online — they sell out.
Lunch is the main meal — take advantage of menú del día deals.
Be careful of pickpockets on Las Ramblas and the metro.
The T-Casual card gives 10 rides on public transport.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Pickpocketing is common in tourist areas — use a front pocket or money belt.

description: The Island of the Gods delivers terraced rice paddies, volcanic peaks, surf breaks, and Hindu temples draped in flowers. Ubud for culture, Canggu for vibes, Uluwatu for cliffs and sunsets.

attractions.name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
attractions.description: Iconic emerald-green rice paddies near Ubud.

attractions.name: Uluwatu Temple
attractions.description: Clifftop temple with Kecak fire dance at sunset.

attractions.name: Ubud Monkey Forest
attractions.description: Sacred forest sanctuary with 700+ macaques.

attractions.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Trek
attractions.description: Pre-dawn hike to watch sunrise over the caldera.

attractions.name: Seminyak Beach Club
attractions.description: Swim, cocktails, and DJ sets overlooking the Indian Ocean.

restaurants.name: Locavore
restaurants.description: Asia's 50 Best — hyper-local tasting menus in Ubud.

restaurants.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka
restaurants.description: Famous roast suckling pig — Anthony Bourdain approved.

restaurants.name: Crate Café
restaurants.description: Canggu's iconic brunch spot — smoothie bowls and flat whites.

hotels.name: Four Seasons at Sayan
hotels.description: Floating above the Ayung River valley — pure luxury in the jungle.

hotels.name: Bisma Eight Ubud
hotels.description: Boutique infinity pool hotel in central Ubud.

hotels.name: Tribal Bali Hostel
hotels.description: Social hostel in Canggu with pool and co-working space.

travel_tips: Rent a scooter (but drive carefully — traffic is chaotic).
Bargain at markets — start at 30% of the asking price.
Carry small notes — change can be hard to get.
Don't touch anyone's head — it's sacred in Hindu culture.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Watch for scooter theft and beware of monkeys stealing belongings.

description: Canals, bicycles, Rembrandt, and gezelligheid. Amsterdam is compact enough to walk everywhere and deep enough to spend weeks. The museum district alone could fill a trip.

attractions.name: Rijksmuseum
attractions.description: Vermeer, Rembrandt, and 8,000 years of Dutch art and history.

attractions.name: Anne Frank House
attractions.description: The hiding place where Anne wrote her diary — deeply moving.

attractions.name: Vondelpark
attractions.description: Amsterdam's green lung — locals picnic, jog, and play music here.

attractions.name: Canal Ring Boat Tour
attractions.description: See the UNESCO-listed canals from the water.

attractions.name: Jordaan Neighbourhood
attractions.description: Narrow streets full of independent boutiques, cafés, and galleries.

restaurants.name: Foodhallen
restaurants.description: Trendy food hall in a former tram depot — 20+ vendors.

restaurants.name: The Pancake Bakery
restaurants.description: Dutch pancakes in a 17th-century canal house.

restaurants.name: Café Winkel 43
restaurants.description: The best apple pie in Amsterdam — fact, not opinion.

hotels.name: Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam
hotels.description: Six canal houses merged into one palatial hotel.

hotels.name: Hotel V Nesplein
hotels.description: Stylish hotel in a great central location.

hotels.name: ClinkNOORD
hotels.description: Design hostel across the IJ river — free ferry to Centraal.

travel_tips: Rent a bike — it's how locals get around.
Book Anne Frank House tickets exactly 6 weeks in advance.
Watch out for bikes when crossing cycle lanes.
An I amsterdam City Card covers museums and transport.
safety_notes: Very safe. Watch for bicycle accidents (look both ways!) and pickpockets at Centraal Station.

description: Sensory overload in the best possible way: spice-scented souks, mosaic-tiled riads, rooftop terraces overlooking the Atlas Mountains. Marrakech feels like stepping into another century.

attractions.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa
attractions.description: The main square — snake charmers, food stalls, and storytellers at night.

attractions.name: Bahia Palace
attractions.description: Stunning 19th-century palace with intricate tilework and gardens.

attractions.name: Majorelle Garden
attractions.description: Yves Saint Laurent's cobalt-blue garden oasis.

attractions.name: The Souks
attractions.description: Labyrinthine markets selling everything from leather to lanterns.

attractions.name: Hammam
attractions.description: Traditional Moroccan bath house — scrub, steam, and massage.

restaurants.name: Café Nomad
restaurants.description: Rooftop views over the souk — modern Moroccan dishes.

restaurants.name: Al Fassia
restaurants.description: Run entirely by women — traditional Moroccan cuisine at its best.

restaurants.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa Food Stalls
restaurants.description: Night market food stalls — grilled meats, snails, fresh juice.

hotels.name: Royal Mansour
hotels.description: King-owned palace hotel — private riads within the hotel.

hotels.name: Riad Yasmine
hotels.description: Instagram-famous riad with a green-tiled plunge pool.

hotels.name: Equity Point Hostel
hotels.description: Former palace turned hostel — incredible rooftop terrace.

travel_tips: Bargain hard in the souks — the first price is 3-5x what you should pay.
Carry small change for tips (guides, bag carriers, toilet attendants).
Drink mint tea — it's the social glue of Morocco.
Book a riad in the medina for the authentic experience.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Beware of aggressive touts and fake guides. Women may experience catcalling.

description: Harbour city with a perfect blend of beaches, bushwalks, food, and culture. The Opera House and Harbour Bridge are just the start — Sydney's best moments are often unplanned.

attractions.name: Sydney Opera House
attractions.description: Jørn Utzon's masterpiece — take a tour or see a performance.

attractions.name: Bondi to Coogee Walk
attractions.description: Spectacular coastal walk past cliffs, rock pools, and beaches.

attractions.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge Climb
attractions.description: Climb to the top of the bridge for 360-degree harbour views.

attractions.name: The Rocks
attractions.description: Historic waterfront precinct with weekend markets and pubs.

attractions.name: Taronga Zoo
attractions.description: Zoo with a view — giraffes against the Sydney skyline.

restaurants.name: Bourke Street Bakery
restaurants.description: Famous pork and fennel sausage rolls — multiple locations.

restaurants.name: Quay
restaurants.description: Fine dining with harbour views — Peter Gilmore's tasting menus.

restaurants.name: Mary's Burgers
restaurants.description: Dive bar meets gourmet smashed burgers in Newtown.

hotels.name: Park Hyatt Sydney
hotels.description: Opera House views from your bathtub — doesn't get better.

hotels.name: Ovolo Woolloomooloo
hotels.description: Converted wharf hotel with harbour views and free minibar.

hotels.name: Wake Up! Sydney
hotels.description: Massive social hostel opposite Central Station.

travel_tips: Opal card for public transport — caps daily spending.
Bondi Beach is overrated for swimming — try Coogee or Bronte instead.
Ferry to Manly is the best cheap activity in the city.
Wear sunscreen — Australian UV is no joke.
safety_notes: Very safe. Swim between the flags at the beach and watch for rip currents.

description: Ancient palaces beside K-pop culture, incredible street food, saunas (jjimjilbangs) where you can sleep overnight, and more beauty products than you can carry home. Seoul is addictive.

attractions.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
attractions.description: Grand Joseon dynasty palace — rent a hanbok for free entry.

attractions.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
attractions.description: Traditional Korean houses on hilly streets — Instagram heaven.

attractions.name: Myeongdong
attractions.description: Shopping district for K-beauty, fashion, and street food.

attractions.name: Hongdae
attractions.description: University district with buskers, clubs, and quirky cafés.

attractions.name: Dragon Hill Spa
attractions.description: Multi-floor jjimjilbang (Korean spa) — try the salt room.

restaurants.name: Gwangjang Market
restaurants.description: Street food market — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and mayak kimbap.

restaurants.name: Jungsik
restaurants.description: Two Michelin stars — modern Korean tasting menus.

restaurants.name: Myeongdong Kyoja
restaurants.description: Famous handmade kalguksu noodles since 1966.

hotels.name: Signiel Seoul
hotels.description: Occupying the top floors of Lotte World Tower — 100th-floor views.

hotels.name: Hotel28 Myeongdong
hotels.description: Stylish boutique hotel in the heart of Myeongdong shopping.

hotels.name: Hongdae Blueprint Hostel
hotels.description: Clean, well-designed hostel in the Hongdae party district.

travel_tips: T-money card works on all transport including taxis.
Korean BBQ is a group activity — don't go alone.
Download Naver Maps — Google Maps doesn't work well in Korea.
Try a hanbok rental for free palace entry and great photos.
safety_notes: Extremely safe — one of the safest cities in the world. You can leave belongings unattended.

description: A sprawling capital with world-class museums, pre-Columbian ruins, and a food scene that rivals any city on earth. Tacos al pastor at 2am might be the single best meal of your life.

attractions.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
attractions.description: The Aztec Sun Stone and one of the world's great museums.

attractions.name: Chapultepec Castle
attractions.description: Hilltop castle overlooking Mexico City — beautiful murals inside.

attractions.name: Xochimilco Canals
attractions.description: Colourful trajineras (boats) on ancient Aztec canals — bring speakers and food.

attractions.name: Coyoacán & Frida Kahlo Museum
attractions.description: Frida's Blue House and the bohemian neighbourhood she loved.

attractions.name: Roma Norte & Condesa
attractions.description: Tree-lined streets, art deco buildings, and Mexico City's best cafés.

restaurants.name: El Huequito
restaurants.description: Birthplace of tacos al pastor — a tiny counter that changed Mexican cuisine.

restaurants.name: Pujol
restaurants.description: World's 50 Best — Enrique Olvera's mole madre has aged for 2,500+ days.

restaurants.name: Mercado Roma
restaurants.description: Upscale food market in Roma Norte — artisanal everything.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Mexico City
hotels.description: Elegant hotel on Paseo de la Reforma with a beautiful courtyard.

hotels.name: Casa Comtesse
hotels.description: Charming boutique in Condesa with a rooftop terrace.

hotels.name: Hostel Home
hotels.description: Clean, friendly hostel in the Zona Rosa area.

travel_tips: Uber is safer and cheaper than taxis — use it everywhere.
Don't drink the tap water — buy garrafones (jugs) from OXXO.
Tuesday is free museum day.
Learn some Spanish — English is less common outside tourist areas.
safety_notes: Safe in tourist areas (Roma, Condesa, Coyoacán, Centro). Use Uber instead of street taxis at night.

description: A fairytale city of Gothic spires, Baroque palaces, and bridges over the Vltava. Prague delivers old-world charm at central European prices — with some of the world's best beer.

attractions.name: Charles Bridge
attractions.description: 14th-century stone bridge lined with Baroque statues — magical at dawn.

attractions.name: Prague Castle
attractions.description: World's largest ancient castle complex — includes St. Vitus Cathedral.

attractions.name: Old Town Square
attractions.description: Astronomical Clock, colourful buildings, and the best people-watching.

attractions.name: Letná Park Beer Garden
attractions.description: Cold Pilsner Urquell with panoramic views over the city.

restaurants.name: Lokál Dlouhááá
restaurants.description: Perfectly poured Pilsner and Czech comfort food — try the svíčková.

restaurants.name: Eska
restaurants.description: Fermentation-focused modern Czech cuisine in a converted factory.

restaurants.name: Naše Maso
restaurants.description: Butcher shop with steak tartare you spread yourself.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel Prague
hotels.description: Stunning views of Prague Castle from the Vltava riverbank.

hotels.name: Hotel Josef
hotels.description: Minimalist design hotel in the Jewish Quarter.

hotels.name: Hostel One Prague
hotels.description: Social hostel with free dinner and pub crawls.

travel_tips: Czech crowns (CZK) get better rates than paying in euros.
Walk Charles Bridge before 7am to avoid crowds.
Prague's beer is cheaper than water — enjoy responsibly.
The metro is fast, clean, and cheap.
safety_notes: Very safe. Minor pickpocket risk on Charles Bridge and in tourist areas.

description: A futuristic desert city of superlatives — tallest building, biggest mall, indoor ski slope. Dubai is extravagant, multicultural, and surprisingly easy to visit on a mid-range budget.

attractions.name: Burj Khalifa
attractions.description: The world's tallest building — sunset views from the 148th floor.

attractions.name: Dubai Creek & Old Souk
attractions.description: Abra boat ride across the creek and gold/spice souks.

attractions.name: Desert Safari
attractions.description: Dune bashing, camel rides, and BBQ dinner under the stars.

attractions.name: Dubai Mall & Aquarium
attractions.description: 1,200 shops, an ice rink, and one of the world's largest aquariums.

restaurants.name: Ravi Restaurant
restaurants.description: Legendary cheap eats in Satwa — open since the 1970s.

restaurants.name: Pierchic
restaurants.description: Seafood restaurant on a pier — Arabian Gulf views.

restaurants.name: Al Ustad Special Kebab
restaurants.description: Hole-in-the-wall kebab shop — the shah ate here.

hotels.name: Burj Al Arab
hotels.description: The world's most luxurious hotel — sail-shaped icon on its own island.

hotels.name: Rove Downtown
hotels.description: Walking distance to Burj Khalifa — great value.

hotels.name: Barsha Backpackers
hotels.description: Clean budget option near Mall of the Emirates.

travel_tips: The metro is modern and covers major attractions.
Dress modestly in malls and public areas.
Friday brunch is a Dubai institution — book one.
Alcohol is only served in licensed hotels and restaurants.
safety_notes: Extremely safe. Very strict laws — be aware of local customs and regulations.

description: Where Table Mountain meets the Atlantic Ocean. Cape Town offers beaches, wine estates, incredible wildlife, and one of the world's most stunning settings — all at favourable exchange rates.

attractions.name: Table Mountain
attractions.description: Hike or take the cable car for panoramic views of the city and ocean.

attractions.name: Cape of Good Hope
attractions.description: The dramatic tip of the Cape Peninsula — wild beauty.

attractions.name: Boulders Beach Penguins
attractions.description: African penguins on a sheltered beach — you can swim with them.

attractions.name: Stellenbosch Wine Route
attractions.description: World-class wine estates 45 minutes from the city.

attractions.name: Robben Island
attractions.description: Nelson Mandela's former prison — a powerful historical experience.

restaurants.name: The Test Kitchen
restaurants.description: Luke Dale-Roberts' innovative tasting menus in Woodstock.

restaurants.name: Mzansi
restaurants.description: Braai (BBQ) and traditional dishes — real South African food.

restaurants.name: Old Biscuit Mill
restaurants.description: Saturday Neighbourgoods Market — artisanal food from 100+ vendors.

hotels.name: One&Only Cape Town
hotels.description: Waterfront luxury with Table Mountain views.

hotels.name: POD Camps Bay
hotels.description: Boutique hotel overlooking Camps Bay beach.

hotels.name: Never@Home
hotels.description: Social hostel in Green Point with rooftop braais.

travel_tips: Rent a car — public transport is limited.
Use Uber rather than metered taxis.
Book Table Mountain cable car online to skip the queue.
The Rand makes Cape Town excellent value for international visitors.
safety_notes: Tourist areas are generally safe. Don't walk alone at night in non-tourist areas. Leave valuables in your hotel safe.

description: A tiny city-state with outsized ambitions — hawker centres serving $3 Michelin meals, futuristic gardens, multicultural neighbourhoods, and the world's best airport. Spotlessly clean and efficient.

attractions.name: Gardens by the Bay
attractions.description: Futuristic supertree grove and cloud forest — stunning at night.

attractions.name: Marina Bay Sands
attractions.description: Iconic rooftop infinity pool and SkyPark observation deck.

attractions.name: Chinatown
attractions.description: Heritage shophouses, temples, and some of the best food in Asia.

attractions.name: Little India
attractions.description: Colourful streets, flower garlands, and fiery South Indian food.

attractions.name: Sentosa Island
attractions.description: Beaches, Universal Studios, and S.E.A. Aquarium.

restaurants.name: Liao Fan Hawker Chan
restaurants.description: World's cheapest Michelin-starred meal — soya sauce chicken rice.

restaurants.name: Jumbo Seafood
restaurants.description: Signature chilli crab — messy, spicy, glorious.

restaurants.name: Tiong Bahru Bakery
restaurants.description: Croissants and kouign-amann in Singapore's hippest neighbourhood.

hotels.name: Raffles Hotel
hotels.description: Colonial-era icon — birthplace of the Singapore Sling.

hotels.name: Naumi Hotel
hotels.description: Rooftop infinity pool with Marina Bay views.

hotels.name: 5footway.inn Project Chinatown
hotels.description: Clean boutique hostel in a heritage shophouse.

travel_tips: MRT (metro) covers everywhere — use a stored-value card.
Hawker centres are where locals eat — cheaper and better than restaurants.
Chewing gum is famously banned — don't bring any.
Indoor air conditioning is fierce — carry a light jacket.
safety_notes: One of the safest cities in the world. Strict laws are taken seriously.

description: A sun-drenched city of seven hills with pastel buildings, melancholic fado music, and custard tarts that will haunt your dreams. Lisbon is Europe's best-value capital — and it knows it.

attractions.name: Belém Tower
attractions.description: 16th-century fortified tower on the Tagus River.

attractions.name: Alfama
attractions.description: The oldest district — narrow alleys, fado bars, and rooftop views.

attractions.name: Tram 28
attractions.description: The iconic yellow tram — a scenic ride through Lisbon's hills.

attractions.name: Time Out Market
attractions.description: Lisbon's best chefs under one roof in a historic market hall.

attractions.name: LX Factory
attractions.description: Creative hub in a former fabric factory — shops, galleries, brunch.

restaurants.name: Pastéis de Belém
restaurants.description: The original pastel de nata since 1837 — warm, flaky, perfect.

restaurants.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
restaurants.description: Best seafood restaurant in Lisbon — end with a steak sandwich.

restaurants.name: A Cevicheria
restaurants.description: Chef Kiko Martins' ceviche bar with a giant octopus hanging from the ceiling.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel Ritz Lisbon
hotels.description: Grand hotel overlooking Eduardo VII Park.

hotels.name: The Lumiares
hotels.description: Converted palace in Bairro Alto with a rooftop terrace.

hotels.name: Goodmorning Hostel
hotels.description: Excellent hostel in Baixa — free walking tours.

travel_tips: Get a Viva Viagem card for public transport.
Wear comfortable shoes — the hills are serious.
Book fado performances at smaller houses for authenticity.
Side trip to Sintra is unmissable (30 minutes by train).
safety_notes: Very safe. Watch for pickpockets on Tram 28 and in Alfama.

description: The Paris of South America dances to a tango beat. Steak, Malbec, bookshops, street art, and football passion — Buenos Aires has soul in a way few cities can match.

attractions.name: La Boca & Caminito
attractions.description: Colourful tin houses and street tango in the most photogenic barrio.

attractions.name: Recoleta Cemetery
attractions.description: Ornate mausoleums including Evita Perón's — hauntingly beautiful.

attractions.name: San Telmo Market
attractions.description: Sunday antiques market with live tango, street food, and vintage finds.

attractions.name: Tango Show at Café Tortoni
attractions.description: Historic café (1858) with intimate tango performances.

restaurants.name: Don Julio
restaurants.description: World's best steak — the 'bife de chorizo' is life-changing.

restaurants.name: El Sanjuanino
restaurants.description: Huge empanadas and humita in a no-frills setting.

restaurants.name: Café San Juan
restaurants.description: Chef Lele Cristóbal's relaxed neighbourhood bistro in San Telmo.

hotels.name: Alvear Palace Hotel
hotels.description: Grand palace hotel in Recoleta — impeccable service.

hotels.name: Mine Hotel
hotels.description: Stylish boutique in Palermo Hollywood.

hotels.name: Milhouse Hostel
hotels.description: Party hostel in a beautiful old building near Plaza de Mayo.

travel_tips: Blue dollar rate gives much better value — check current rates.
Steak for dinner is customary around 9-10pm.
Subte (metro) is fast for getting around the centre.
Learn a few tango steps — milongas (dance halls) welcome beginners.
safety_notes: Generally safe in tourist areas. Avoid flashing valuables and use registered taxis or Uber.

description: History, culture, and an absurdly good food scene hidden behind a reputation for bad weather. London delivers world-class museums (free!), theatre, parks, and pubs with real ales.

attractions.name: British Museum
attractions.description: The Rosetta Stone, Egyptian mummies, and centuries of global history — free.

attractions.name: Tower of London
attractions.description: 1,000-year-old fortress housing the Crown Jewels.

attractions.name: Borough Market
attractions.description: London's oldest food market — cheese, bread, oysters, and more.

attractions.name: West End Theatre
attractions.description: World-class musicals and plays in Theatreland.

attractions.name: Hyde Park & Kensington Gardens
attractions.description: Central London's green escape — rowing, swimming, or just sitting.

restaurants.name: Dishoom
restaurants.description: Bombay-inspired café — the bacon naan roll is legendary.

restaurants.name: Bao
restaurants.description: Steamed buns with inventive fillings — worth the queue.

restaurants.name: St. JOHN
restaurants.description: Fergus Henderson's nose-to-tail pioneering — roasted bone marrow is the signature.

hotels.name: The Savoy
hotels.description: Legendary riverside hotel — art deco grandeur since 1889.

hotels.name: The Z Hotel Soho
hotels.description: Compact but stylish rooms in the heart of Soho.

hotels.name: Generator London
hotels.description: Massive hostel near Russell Square with a bar and events.

travel_tips: Oyster card or contactless payment for transport — daily caps apply.
Most major museums are free — plan around them.
Queue for day seats at the National Theatre for cheap tickets.
Pubs close at 11pm (some earlier) — plan accordingly.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Watch for pickpockets on the Tube and in busy tourist areas.

description: Blue-domed churches, white-washed buildings cascading down volcanic cliffs, and the most photographed sunsets in the world. Santorini is romantic, dramatic, and utterly unforgettable.

attractions.name: Oia Sunset
attractions.description: The world's most famous sunset — arrive early for a spot.

attractions.name: Fira to Oia Hike
attractions.description: 10km cliffside trail with caldera views the entire way.

attractions.name: Red Beach
attractions.description: Dramatic red volcanic cliffs meeting deep blue water.

attractions.name: Akrotiri Archaeological Site
attractions.description: A Minoan Pompeii — ancient city preserved under volcanic ash.

attractions.name: Wine Tasting
attractions.description: Volcanic soil produces unique Assyrtiko wines — visit Santo Wines.

restaurants.name: Ammoudi Fish Taverna
restaurants.description: Fresh fish by the water at the bottom of 300 steps from Oia.

restaurants.name: Metaxy Mas
restaurants.description: Off-the-beaten-path taverna — locals' favourite.

restaurants.name: Lucky's Souvlaki
restaurants.description: Best cheap eat in Fira — massive pita wraps.

hotels.name: Mystique
hotels.description: Luxury cave hotel in Oia with infinity pool caldera views.

hotels.name: Aethrio Hotel
hotels.description: Charming family-run hotel in Oia with great views.

hotels.name: Caveland Hostel
hotels.description: Stay in an actual cave — unique hostel in Karterados.

travel_tips: Visit in May or September to avoid cruise-ship crowds.
Rent an ATV to explore the island — roads are narrow for cars.
Sunset in Oia is crowded — try Imerovigli for fewer people.
Book caldera-view accommodation well in advance.
safety_notes: Very safe. The main risk is sunburn and the steep stairs after wine tasting.

description: Mountains meet ocean in Canada's most livable city. Ski in the morning, kayak in the afternoon, then eat world-class sushi. Vancouver's natural setting is jaw-dropping.

attractions.name: Stanley Park
attractions.description: 1,000-acre urban park — seawall walk, totem poles, and beaches.

attractions.name: Grouse Mountain
attractions.description: Gondola ride with city views — hiking in summer, skiing in winter.

attractions.name: Granville Island
attractions.description: Public market, art studios, and craft breweries on a former industrial island.

attractions.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge
attractions.description: Sway 230 feet above a temperate rainforest canyon.

restaurants.name: Miku
restaurants.description: Aburi (flame-seared) sushi overlooking the harbour.

restaurants.name: Japadog
restaurants.description: Japanese-style hot dogs — a Vancouver street food icon.

restaurants.name: Vij's
restaurants.description: No-reservation Indian restaurant that's worth every minute of the wait.

hotels.name: Fairmont Pacific Rim
hotels.description: Luxury waterfront hotel with mountain views.

hotels.name: Skwachàys Lodge
hotels.description: Indigenous arts hotel — each room designed by a different artist.

hotels.name: HI Vancouver Central
hotels.description: Great downtown location near Granville Street.

travel_tips: The SeaBus to North Vancouver is a beautiful (and cheap) harbour ride.
Bring layers — weather changes quickly.
Dim sum in Richmond rivals Hong Kong.
The city is very bike-friendly — rent one.
safety_notes: Very safe. Some areas of the Downtown Eastside are best avoided at night.

description: Christ the Redeemer, Copacabana, samba rhythms, and the world's biggest party (Carnival). Rio has an infectious joy that's impossible to resist — plus some of the most dramatic urban scenery anywhere.

attractions.name: Christ the Redeemer
attractions.description: The 30m statue atop Corcovado — city-wide views.

attractions.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
attractions.description: Cable car to the summit — best at sunset.

attractions.name: Copacabana Beach
attractions.description: The world's most famous beach — 4km of sand and people-watching.

attractions.name: Santa Teresa
attractions.description: Bohemian hillside neighbourhood — art galleries, bars, and colonial architecture.

attractions.name: Lapa Arches
attractions.description: Friday night samba clubs under the colonial aqueduct — Rio's best nightlife.

restaurants.name: Confeitaria Colombo
restaurants.description: Stunning belle-époque café — afternoon tea since 1894.

restaurants.name: Aprazível
restaurants.description: Treehouse restaurant in Santa Teresa — tropical garden setting.

restaurants.name: Bar do Mineiro
restaurants.description: Cold chopp beer and feijoada (black bean stew) in Santa Teresa.

hotels.name: Belmond Copacabana Palace
hotels.description: Grand dame of Copacabana — Art Deco luxury since 1923.

hotels.name: Mama Ruisa
hotels.description: Charming boutique in Santa Teresa with city views.

hotels.name: El Misti Hostel Copacabana
hotels.description: Rooftop hostel two blocks from Copacabana Beach.

travel_tips: Don't bring valuables to the beach.
Uber is the safest transport option.
Learn some Portuguese — it goes a long way.
Carnival happens in February/March — book months ahead.
safety_notes: Tourist areas are generally safe during the day. Avoid favelas unless with a reputable guide. Don't walk on beaches at night.

description: The adventure capital of the world — bungee jumping, skydiving, jet boats, and skiing — all set against impossibly beautiful Southern Alps and Lake Wakatipu scenery.

attractions.name: Bungee Jump (Kawarau Bridge)
attractions.description: The original commercial bungee — 43m above the river.

attractions.name: Milford Sound Day Trip
attractions.description: Fiord cruise through towering peaks and waterfalls.

attractions.name: Skyline Gondola & Luge
attractions.description: Ride up for lake views, then luge down the mountain.

attractions.name: Remarkables Ski Field
attractions.description: World-class skiing with stunning mountain scenery.

restaurants.name: Fergburger
restaurants.description: The world's most famous burger joint — queue any time, day or night.

restaurants.name: Rata
restaurants.description: Josh Emett's fine dining using local ingredients.

restaurants.name: The Bathhouse
restaurants.description: Waterfront dining on the lake — stunning setting.

hotels.name: Eichardt's Private Hotel
hotels.description: Lakefront boutique luxury — Queenstown's finest.

hotels.name: Novotel Queenstown
hotels.description: Lake views and central location — good mid-range pick.

hotels.name: Adventure Queenstown Hostel
hotels.description: Social hostel with sauna and mountain views.

travel_tips: Book activities online in advance — especially Milford Sound.
Winter (June-August) is ski season; summer (December-February) is hiking season.
A car is essential for day trips.
Fergburger is open until 5am — perfect post-adventure fuel.
safety_notes: Very safe. Weather can change rapidly in the mountains — always be prepared.

description: The only city on two continents, Istanbul layers 2,000 years of Byzantine and Ottoman history with a buzzing modern art scene, kebabs at 3am, and tea on every corner.

attractions.name: Hagia Sophia
attractions.description: 1,500-year-old cathedral-turned-mosque — architectural wonder.

attractions.name: Grand Bazaar
attractions.description: One of the world's oldest covered markets — 4,000 shops.

attractions.name: Blue Mosque
attractions.description: Iconic 17th-century mosque with six minarets and blue İznik tiles.

attractions.name: Bosphorus Cruise
attractions.description: Ferry between Europe and Asia — Ottoman palaces on both shores.

attractions.name: Basilica Cistern
attractions.description: Underground 6th-century water storage — atmospheric and mysterious.

restaurants.name: Çiya Sofrası
restaurants.description: Regional Anatolian dishes you won't find anywhere else — Kadıköy gem.

restaurants.name: Karaköy Güllüoğlu
restaurants.description: The best baklava in Istanbul since 1949.

restaurants.name: Mikla
restaurants.description: Rooftop fine dining with Bosphorus views — Turkish-Scandinavian fusion.

hotels.name: Four Seasons at Sultanahmet
hotels.description: Former prison turned luxury hotel — steps from Hagia Sophia.

hotels.name: Hotel Empress Zoe
hotels.description: Charming boutique with archaeological ruins in the garden.

hotels.name: Cheers Hostel
hotels.description: Rooftop with Blue Mosque views — unbeatable for the price.

travel_tips: Get an Istanbulkart for all public transport.
The Asian side (Kadıköy) has better food and fewer tourists.
Bargain in the Grand Bazaar — never pay the first price.
Turkish breakfast is a ceremony — try it at a kahvaltıcı.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Normal tourist precautions apply. Some areas of Taksim can be rowdy at night.

description: Japan's cultural heart — 2,000 temples and shrines, geisha districts, bamboo groves, and the most exquisite food presentation on earth. Kyoto moves at a gentler pace than Tokyo.

attractions.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
attractions.description: Thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the mountainside.

attractions.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
attractions.description: Towering bamboo forest — arrive at dawn for the best experience.

attractions.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
attractions.description: Gold-leaf temple reflected in a mirror pond — quintessential Kyoto.

attractions.name: Gion District
attractions.description: Traditional geisha quarter — preserved machiya townhouses.

attractions.name: Nishiki Market
attractions.description: Kyoto's kitchen — 400 years of food stalls and specialties.

restaurants.name: Nishiki Warai
restaurants.description: Okonomiyaki (savoury pancakes) near Nishiki Market.

restaurants.name: Kikunoi
restaurants.description: Three Michelin stars — the pinnacle of traditional Japanese cuisine.

restaurants.name: Ippudo Ramen
restaurants.description: Tonkotsu ramen chain — always reliable and quick.

hotels.name: Aman Kyoto
hotels.description: Hidden forest retreat — minimalist luxury.

hotels.name: Hotel Kanra Kyoto
hotels.description: Modern machiya-style rooms with private onsen baths.

hotels.name: Piece Hostel Kyoto
hotels.description: Design hostel near the station — excellent facilities.

travel_tips: Rent a bicycle — Kyoto is flat and bike-friendly.
Visit temples early morning to avoid crowds.
Buy a one-day bus pass for ¥700.
Fushimi Inari is open 24 hours — midnight visits are magical.
safety_notes: Extremely safe. Be respectful at temples — follow the signs and etiquette.

description: Gateway to otherworldly landscapes — geysers, glaciers, volcanoes, and the Northern Lights. Reykjavik itself is a colourful, creative capital with an outsized music and food scene.

attractions.name: Golden Circle
attractions.description: Day trip: Þingvellir, Geysir, and Gullfoss waterfall.

attractions.name: Blue Lagoon
attractions.description: Geothermal spa in a lava field — milky blue water.

attractions.name: Northern Lights Tour
attractions.description: Chase the aurora borealis from September to March.

attractions.name: Hallgrímskirkja
attractions.description: Reykjavik's landmark church — tower views over the city.

restaurants.name: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur
restaurants.description: The best hot dog stand in the world — Bill Clinton approved.

restaurants.name: Grillið
restaurants.description: Fine dining at the top of the Saga Hotel — tasting menus with a view.

restaurants.name: Hlemmur Mathöll
restaurants.description: Food hall with Icelandic and international vendors.

hotels.name: The Retreat at Blue Lagoon
hotels.description: Built into a lava flow — private lagoon access.

hotels.name: Canopy by Hilton Reykjavik
hotels.description: Central location with an excellent restaurant.

hotels.name: KEX Hostel
hotels.description: Quirky hostel in a former biscuit factory — great bar.

travel_tips: Rent a 4WD for the Ring Road.
Iceland is expensive — bring snacks and a water bottle.
Tap water is glacier-fed and delicious.
Summer has 24 hours of daylight — bring an eye mask.
safety_notes: Extremely safe. Weather changes rapidly — always check road conditions and never drive off marked roads.

description: Chaotic, charming, and delicious. Hanoi's Old Quarter buzzes with scooters and street food stalls — sit on a tiny plastic stool, eat the best pho of your life, and fall in love with this city.

attractions.name: Old Quarter
attractions.description: 36 ancient streets named after the goods they sold — now pure energy.

attractions.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
attractions.description: The heart of Hanoi — morning tai chi, evening strolls.

attractions.name: Temple of Literature
attractions.description: Vietnam's first university (1070) — beautiful courtyards.

attractions.name: Train Street
attractions.description: Houses inches from the railway — trains pass through twice daily.

attractions.name: Ha Long Bay Day Trip
attractions.description: Limestone karsts rising from emerald water — UNESCO World Heritage.

restaurants.name: Pho Gia Truyen
restaurants.description: The city's most famous pho — open since 1977.

restaurants.name: Bún Chả Hương Liên
restaurants.description: Where Obama ate with Bourdain — grilled pork with noodles.

restaurants.name: Bia Hoi Corner
restaurants.description: Cheap fresh beer (bia hoi) and street food — Old Quarter institution.

hotels.name: Sofitel Legend Metropole
hotels.description: French colonial legend — writers and diplomats since 1901.

hotels.name: Hanoi La Siesta Hotel
hotels.description: Beautiful boutique in the Old Quarter — outstanding service.

hotels.name: Old Quarter View Hostel
hotels.description: Rooftop views and tiny prices — classic Hanoi backpacker spot.

travel_tips: Cross the road with confidence — scooters will go around you.
Street food is the best food — eat where locals eat.
Grab (ride-hailing) is the easiest way to get around.
Overnight train to Sapa is a great adventure.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Watch for motorbike bag snatching and negotiate prices before services.

description: A Caribbean colonial gem — colourful buildings, cobblestoned streets, salsa-filled nights, and ceviche on the beach. Cartagena's walled old town feels like stepping into a Gabriel García Márquez novel.

attractions.name: Walled City (Centro Histórico)
attractions.description: UNESCO-listed colonial quarter — flower-draped balconies and plazas.

attractions.name: Castillo de San Felipe
attractions.description: Massive 17th-century fortress with underground tunnels.

attractions.name: Rosario Islands
attractions.description: Boat trip to white-sand islands with crystal-clear water.

attractions.name: Getsemaní
attractions.description: Street art, local bars, and Cartagena's coolest neighbourhood.

restaurants.name: La Cevichería
restaurants.description: Best ceviche in the city — Obama ate here too.

restaurants.name: El Boliche
restaurants.description: Cheap lunch counter — arroz con coco and fried fish.

restaurants.name: Carmen
restaurants.description: Latin America's 50 Best — elegant colonial house setting.

hotels.name: Casa San Agustín
hotels.description: Boutique luxury in a 17th-century convent.

hotels.name: Hotel Casa Lola
hotels.description: Colourful boutique in the walled city — great rooftop.

hotels.name: Media Luna Hostel
hotels.description: Party hostel in Getsemaní with pool and rum punch.

travel_tips: Negotiate taxi fares before getting in.
Carry small bills — change is always an issue.
Drink lots of water — the humidity is intense.
Take a salsa class — it's the social language of Colombia.
safety_notes: Tourist areas are safe. Avoid deserted streets at night. Don't wear flashy jewellery.

description: Imperial palaces, Klimt masterpieces, coffeehouses where you can linger for hours, and the world's best classical music scene. Vienna is sophisticated without being stuffy.

attractions.name: Schönbrunn Palace
attractions.description: 1,441-room Habsburg summer palace — gardens are free.

attractions.name: Belvedere Palace
attractions.description: Houses Klimt's The Kiss — one of the world's most famous paintings.

attractions.name: Vienna State Opera
attractions.description: Standing tickets for €4 — world-class opera at budget prices.

attractions.name: Naschmarkt
attractions.description: Vienna's biggest market — Middle Eastern food, wine bars, vintage stalls.

restaurants.name: Café Central
restaurants.description: Historic coffeehouse where Freud and Trotsky once debated.

restaurants.name: Figlmüller
restaurants.description: Vienna's most famous Wiener Schnitzel — bigger than the plate.

restaurants.name: Bitzinger Würstelstand
restaurants.description: Gourmet sausage stand behind the Opera — champagne and käsekrainer.

hotels.name: Hotel Sacher
hotels.description: Home of the original Sachertorte — imperial luxury.

hotels.name: Hotel Capricorno
hotels.description: Central location near St. Stephen's Cathedral.

hotels.name: Wombat's City Hostel
hotels.description: Near Naschmarkt — good base with bar and terrace.

travel_tips: Vienna City Card covers transport and museum discounts.
Standing tickets at the Opera are the best deal in Vienna.
Try Sturm (partially fermented grape juice) in autumn.
Coffeehouse culture is UNESCO-listed — take your time.
safety_notes: One of the safest capitals in Europe. Minimal crime — enjoy the city freely.

description: Gateway to Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley. Cusco blends Incan ruins with Spanish colonial architecture, vibrant textiles, and Andean cuisine at 3,400m altitude.

attractions.name: Machu Picchu
attractions.description: The Lost City of the Incas — one of the New Seven Wonders.

attractions.name: Sacred Valley
attractions.description: Incan terraces, colourful markets, and mountain villages.

attractions.name: Plaza de Armas
attractions.description: Cusco's main square — colonial churches and Incan foundations.

attractions.name: Rainbow Mountain
attractions.description: Striped mineral mountain at 5,200m — challenging but stunning.

attractions.name: San Pedro Market
attractions.description: Local market with fresh juices, alpaca products, and cheap lunches.

restaurants.name: Central (Lima satellite)
restaurants.description: Virgilio Martínez's altitude-themed tasting menu.

restaurants.name: Jack's Café
restaurants.description: Huge breakfasts — fuel for altitude and hiking.

restaurants.name: Chicha by Gastón Acurio
restaurants.description: Elevated Andean cuisine in a beautiful colonial setting.

hotels.name: Belmond Hotel Monasterio
hotels.description: Converted 16th-century monastery — oxygen-enriched rooms for altitude.

hotels.name: Antigua Casona
hotels.description: Colonial house with a courtyard — quiet and central.

hotels.name: Wild Rover Hostel
hotels.description: Famous party hostel — social but not for light sleepers.

travel_tips: Acclimatize for 2 days before doing anything strenuous.
Coca tea helps with altitude sickness.
Book Machu Picchu tickets well in advance — daily limits apply.
Trek the Inca Trail (4 days) or take the train — both are incredible.
safety_notes: Generally safe. Altitude sickness is the main risk — take it slowly. Watch for taxi scams.
